llm.summary: This is a Mermaid diagram guidance skill with normal documentation examples, but its HTML rendering snippets need care around third-party scripts and untrusted diagrams.

dimensions.detail: HTML rendering and interactive links fit the stated diagram purpose, but the documented securityLevel: 'loose' and very high maxTextSize setting are not appropriate defaults for rendering untrusted or user-supplied diagrams.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill documents a jsDelivr Mermaid import and an npm global install for Mermaid CLI; these are purpose-aligned third-party dependency examples, but the artifact does not warn users about network and supply-chain implications.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger list uses broad terms like diagram, model, architecture, and flow, which could invoke the skill more often than ideal, but the loaded instructions remain scoped to Mermaid diagram assistance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package consists of Markdown reference files with mode 644; I found no executable scripts, persistence hooks, background workers, memory writes, credential access, or privilege escalation behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact is focused on creating Mermaid diagrams, with syntax examples, reference material, styling guidance, export commands, and HTML integration examples; I found no hidden data collection, unrelated authority, or system-control instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install is reasonable for Mermaid diagram help. Be careful before copying the HTML snippets into production or sensitive environments: prefer a pinned or self-hosted Mermaid dependency, avoid securityLevel: 'loose' for untrusted diagrams, keep Mermaid input size limits conservative, and review any interactive links in generated diagrams.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad triggers are real, but they point to diagram-related work and do not add hidden authority or non-diagram behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: The English-identifier troubleshooting note is a documentation-quality and compatibility concern, not a security or privilege concern.
[EA2] expected: The cited auto-deploy text is a node label inside an example deployment flowchart, not an instruction for the agent to deploy software or take autonomous action.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The Gantt versus data-visualization wording is inconsistent documentation, but it does not create hidden behavior or unsafe capability.
[SQP-2] expected: The CDN import is expected for an HTML Mermaid example, though users should understand it loads third-party JavaScript from the network.
[SQP-2] expected: The later HTML template repeats the same jsDelivr dependency; this is disclosed in the code but lacks nearby privacy or supply-chain guidance.
[T09] unexpected: The loose Mermaid rendering configuration is the main real safety caveat; it is documentation users may copy, not code the skill executes itself, so it warrants guidance rather than a Review verdict.
